that her calorie intake is adequate.
Laboratory Data Relevant laboratory tests to be monitored are fasting fat-soluble vitamin levels 
(PIVKA-II and vitamins A, D, and E) annually and iron studies if there is a concern for anemia. 
Albumin and pre-albumin levels can be affected by acute infection and therefore may not reliably 
detect a change in nutritional status. HgA1c may be useful in detecting a history of hyperglycemia, 
however, sometimes can be falsely low in patients with CF and therefore cannot rule out a diagnosis 
of CF-related diabetes. A 2-hour oral glucose tolerance test should be checked annually in all 
patients over the age of 10 years to screen for CF-related diabetes.
